title: Games With Ai?
author: lol_aarav
selftext: So uh I'm making a simulation heavy/cpu heavy colony game kind of a mix of oxygen not included with factiro and has elements of politics and other survival mechanisms so the thing is i am a very bad artist lol, though the game is based on 2D pixel art style, is it A good decision to push assets with Ai ? Or should I learn to draw too i can try but I'm not a good artist and that will tank the visuals. I took some sample art from Ai and i honestly couldn't even tell if that was Ai because it got the pixels very right

comments.author: bettertagsweretaken
comments.body:
So long as you have a cohesive vision and don't compromise with AI generative art, people can't tell. AI is VERY GOOD these days at producing character art. 

https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMqeM_nHxab0&si=pZqmSOkDi6ROTaNG

comments.author: Acceptable_Movie6712
comments.body: I would lean on making art yourself. If it’s 2D you can buy sprite assets. I think people can understand vibe coding a game, but you’ll get less love from gamers if everything - especially the art - is made with AI. You need to have your “art” assets like graphics, music and sfx non ai generated.

replies.author: HighreachGrit
replies.body:
I would argue this all day man. @op don't try to push your own art if it truly is bad, it'll kill your curb appeal and even though everyone SAYS they don't care about graphics and just want a good game, what they actually do is instant skip your store page without reading if the see bad art. 

This is not to say I recommend AI art as there's a witch hunt on. In your case maybe you can hire someone or purchase assets or find some for free. Or get good at art yourself but that takes a long time generally

comments.author: SpaghettiMan247
comments.body:
I use ai art for now, I can draw but don’t have time.  I do usually draw new characters as concept art though. 

If my game gains traction I might redo all the art towards the end, for now the project continues to move forward.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: make your art appealing and consistent and it doesn't matter if it's AI

comments.author: KhaosPT
comments.body: If it looks good and doesn't look like someone tried to one shot and did not make any effort, then there will be no issue.

comments.author: Kraftwerkzeug
comments.body: Honestly use whatever tools you want. If your game is good then it doesn’t matter.  AI is in everything now. It’s the way it’s going.

comments.author: Onye_Nacho
comments.body:
It truly depends on the circumstance, notably the art style you want, and the scope and vision of the game. If you were working on a cartoony short game like an arcade shooter for instance, then you may be better of investing the time creating the art manually. Since you want a complex colony simulator, that will take forever to learn everything manually, so using GAI tools to your **advantage and responsibility** is your best chance to expedite this effectively and efficiently. Ignore the nay-sayers against GAI; no matter the hatred, this tool is the most important and reliable software known to humanity and is crucial if you are a solo game developer with little-to-no funding power, much less to hire some probably self-entitled or over talented and overpaid creator who may probably pester, frustrate, harass, or betray you later, losing more valuable time, money, morale, and sanity in the process. Good luck even trying to find free talent willing to help you, especially for ambitious projects of this scope (colony simulator is a huge deal to work on for free) - that's a usually rare feat to maintain. Almost anyone you seek to recruit into your team will want your money first.

Regardless, it is still always a good idea to invest some time to improve your own manual creative talents (art and otherwise as necessary). They can be reliable as fail-safes when matters go wrong in your game development endeavor (eg. GAI tool or service malfunctions or kicks the bucket).  
  
Summary:  
Never rely fully on GAI software, and never work too hard like an outdated fool. No matter what the wishful thinker game devs will tell you, NO ONE will truly care how long and how much you've suffered to make your decade-long video game by the turn of its release (if not by the playtest phase). I learned the latter the hard way from the last decade into this one, and I vowed never to repeat that mistake again.

Work smart, not hard.

replies.author: lol_aarav
replies.body: Aye thanks man i appreciate your efforts in making this comment! best one yet

replies.author: Onye_Nacho
replies.body: Welcome. Sometimes its always give new tech/features a chance whenever possible. You'll never know if it may become the difference that can improve your career and/or hobbies than ever before.
